deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematical derivation. It is a heavily revised pencil draft of a referee's report (Gutachten/Beurtheilung) on an essay submitted for a mathematical prize question of the (Göttingen) Philosophical Faculty. The essay carried the motto 'Tanto uberiores sunt notae, quanto magis exprimunt rerum relationes'. Given the bundle 'R.Ellipsoid', the prize question presumably concerned fluid motion in the setting of Riemann's 1861 paper on the motion of a homogeneous liquid ellipsoid. The topic is clearly hydrodynamics: 'Lagrange'sche Gleichungen', 'Lagrange'sche Betrachtungsweise der Bewegung', 'Wirbelbewegung'.

The top lines are a detached fragment, probably an insertion for the report. It refers to the Lagrangian equations being satisfied simultaneously ('die Lagrange'schen Gleichungen gleichzeitig befriedigt werden, so'). Above it is an interlinear note: '…die gleichfalls auf Lagrange'sche Co[ordinaten?]…'. A reference to '§. 14. 15.' of the essay stands at the top right.

The report itself makes the following points.
(1) The essay testifies to the author's diligence, his acquaintance with the methods developed by recent mathematicians, and the skill he has acquired in handling them.
(2) This shows especially in §6, which sets out an elegant method for obtaining the equations in Lagrangian form. The method gives this way of treating the motion, likewise referred to Lagrangian coordinates, in a fully general/arbitrary coordinate system; the last word is uncertain.
(3) In the following development of the general laws (struck variants mention the general laws of vortex motion, §§7–9), the Lagrangian viewpoint is abandoned. As a consequence, the connection between the equations and the laws in question escaped the author, as did the investigations presented in §§14–15; the reading is uncertain.
(4) Since the author nevertheless starts from the Lagrangian equations in his attempt, this part of the essay fulfils the task essentially. A parenthesis refers to a defect or abrupt break in §9, and to the part being independent of it.

The struck lines at the bottom ('Referent…', 'dieser Theil … der Aufgabe') begin the verdict. The next page continues it: the imperfection in this part would not be a sufficient reason against awarding the prize, and could be removed by a revision that would gain in brevity and sharpness. Inaccuracies in §§3–8 are attributed to hasty writing.

In modern terms, the scientific content is the issue of Lagrangian (material) versus Eulerian descriptions of fluid flow. There is also the derivation of Helmholtz's vortex laws (1858), which are naturally expressed via Lagrangian/Cauchy invariants. The referee criticises the author for leaving the Lagrangian frame and thereby missing the connection with those laws.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an administrative referee report draft with no new mathematics. It is of modest archival interest: it shows Riemann's emphasis on the Lagrangian description and its link to vortex laws. The identity of the prize essay is unclear to me.
transcription_corrections: Opening of the report likely reads 'Die Abhandlung giebt ein rühmliches Zeugniß von dem Fleisse des Verfassers, von seiner Bekanntschaft mit den von den neueren Mathematikern ausgebildeten Methoden und der erworbenen Gewandtheit in der Handhabung derselben', not 'zeugt im Ganzen'.
Top-right reference 'S. 14. 15.' is '§. 14. 15.' (sections of the essay).

Top interlinear note 'auf Lagrange Covariante' more plausibly reads 'auf Lagrange'sche Coordinaten'. Likewise 'die gleichfalls auf Lagrange basirt wird' probably reads 'auf Lagrange'sche Coordinaten bezogen wird'.
'für ein ganz bestimmtes Coordinatensystem' may rather be 'für ein ganz beliebiges Coordinatensystem' (general coordinates).
The inserted word read as 'Drei[?]' above 'Motto' is doubtful. The phrase is simply 'mit dem Motto'.
'34' in the right margin (twice) is the folio number, not text.
